source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter III, §17 Attacking without the Aid of Knights, Example 45

steps.title: A beautiful position
steps.source: White has a beautiful position, but still he had better gain some material, if he can, before Black consolidates his defensive position.

narration.say: White has a beautiful position, with both rooks on the h-file.
Still, he had better gain some material before Black consolidates.

feedback.*: A rook takes the knight on h6.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Sacrifice the exchange.
exercise.wrong: A rook takes the knight on h6.

feedback.*: The bishop on e3 takes on h6 with check.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check with the bishop.
exercise.wrong: The bishop on e3 takes on h6 with check.
exercise.success: 2. Bxh6, check. If Nxh6, Rxh6 and Black is helpless. The king goes to e7.

narration.say: Queen to h7, check. King to e8.
Queen takes the knight on g8, check. King to d7.
Queen to h7, check, and the black queen blocks on e7.

feedback.*: The bishop can attack the queen on e7.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Attack the black queen with the bishop.
exercise.wrong: The bishop can attack the queen on e7.

narration.say: Rook takes back, check. King to e8.
And rook takes the rook on a7. Black resigned.
Rooks and bishops attacked together with the queen. No knights took part.
